correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the complete quotient-Cayley/finite Walsh proof: the \(n+1\) generating classes are edge-transitive; even-subset characters diagonalize the Laplacian at \(2|S|\); exact beta integrals give antisymmetric strictly decreasing edge-source potentials; ordinary-coordinate currents sum to \(n/2\); antipodal matching currents reduce by majority-binomial cancellation to \(1-4^{-k}\binom{2k}{k}\); trace of the orthogonal cut projection fixes the diagonal and the cycle norm. Exact Fraction checks reconstructed 22,520 spectral edge currents in dimensions three through eleven and six independently solved grounded-Laplacian columns in dimensions three through five. Computations test only finite instances and do not substitute for the written all-dimensions proof. Graph is simple and canonical for every integer dimension at least five; all signs and endpoints are justified.

originality.rationale: The claim supplies an exact all-dimension central-binomial formula for two canonical orthogonal edge projection norms of antipodally augmented binary cubes and a strict quantitative excess over the known ordinary Hamming-cube norm. The closest full-text prior work treats the unaugmented graph; an inspected folded-cube symmetry paper studies unrelated distinguishing invariants. Indexed results about Walsh free-space projections or folded-cube topology do not imply this edge-cut norm. Small-dimension graph classes are excluded from the novelty range. Less-indexed literature remains a risk.
residual_risks: A different equivalent formulation may occur in unindexed finite electrical-network or resistance literature, despite no covering statement in inspected sources.
The exact n=3 and n=4 folded graphs have additional classical presentations; no independent novelty claim is made for those values.
No independent external expert validation or exhaustive bibliographic uniqueness proof has been performed.

value.rationale: The general exact norm law is motivated by the 2023 ordinary-hypercube benchmark and the natural antipodal perfect-matching augmentation. It quantitatively determines whether, and by how much, this insertion changes canonical Banach cut/cycle norms for an unbounded dimension family. The central-binomial majority identity and parity plateau identify nontrivial structure not available from a generic finite matrix calculation. The statement is natural, extensible and of exact all-dimensions value, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
